description: Filters of the Lick Observatory (Mount Hamilton) filter collection: narrow-, medium- and broad-band filters kept at the 3-meter and 1-meter telescopes and available for borrowing (Mount Hamilton Filter List). The curves are the measured transmission tables published by the observatory (techdocs/filters/data/); the broad filters 3300_1150, 3500_800, 3600_600, 4000_650 and 7400hp are labelled 'Measured December 2010 at UCSC' and cover 200-2000 nm. B, V, R, I and Rs come from the observatory's 'Transmission tables for our B, V, R, I, and Rs filters' (phot_filt_curves.html), whose values 'were read off by eye i(not ours) from spectrophotometer tracings' [sic] (owner's caveat: 'We do not guarantee their accuracy.'); the page says the BVRI filters 'were made according to the prescription given by Bessel (PASP 1990, 102, 1181)' and Rs 'is the Spinrad night-sky suppression filter'.
facility_description: Lick Observatory on Mount Hamilton, California (University of California Observatories / Lick Observatory, as headed on the filter-list page).

notes: Owner host mthamilton.ucolick.org timed out on 26 Oct 2026 (http and https); each data file is a single Internet Archive id_ capture (timestamps in the band Sources and in R7/X4/downloads/LICK/cdx_*.txt). Wavelengths in Angstrom (2010 UCSC files converted from nm, % to fraction). The 2010 broad-band files include the measured infrared transmission to 2000 nm (e.g. 4000_650 rises to 57 % at 2000 nm); SVO's copies stop near 750 nm, so pivot wavelengths differ from SVO for these bands. DetectorType photon assumed; filter transmission only. 4000_650 (2026-11-12): the curve is Lick's scan of its 4000/650 filter over 200-2000 nm ('Measured December 2010 at UCSC'). Lick's filter list says 'Red leak starting about 7000A', and the leak rises above the main peak (57 % at 2000 nm against 38.5 % at 3980 A), so a centre or width taken over the whole curve describes the leak. SVO's record is the main band only (3300-7500 A). 3650_80 (2026-11-12): the curve is Lick's 2012 scan (M. Clendenin) of the filter its list calls 3650/80, whose measured value Lick gives as 3715/66 (https://mthamilton.ucolick.org/techdocs/filters/f3380.html); the filter transmits only about 4 %. 3870_30 (2026-11-12): the curve is Lick's 2012 scan (E. Gates) of its 3870/30 filter, which Lick lists as 'degraded, wavelength shifted significantly redwards' (https://mthamilton.ucolick.org/techdocs/filters/f3380.html). 6570_70 (2026-11-12): Lick's own filter list gives the measured value of its 6570/70 filter as 7142/46, the same as its 7141/50 filter (https://mthamilton.ucolick.org/techdocs/filters/f6500.html, f7000.html), and Lick's 6570/70 file is the 7141/50 curve point for point (max |dT| 0.001). The curve is not a 6570/70 passband; Lick does not say which filter the scan is.
